subject: Options for mid-contract uplift, payment split, and amendment
messages:
From: Asha Rao <asha@heliomed.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-contract uplift — proposal and payment questions

Hey Markus,

Quick context: our product team has pushed an earlier AI rollout and we're likely to need an additional 600k tokens/month starting May 1 — effectively a ~40% uplift over our current committed volume. We want to avoid a full renewal right now but need predictable pricing and a path to co-term the uplift with our Feb renewal next year.

Two specific asks:
- Can you provide pricing for the uplift as a separate add-on (monthly) vs. an annualized pro-rate for the remaining 10 months?
- We also need to understand payment options: can HelioMed split the uplift payment over two invoices (May + Nov) or do you require immediate full payment?

Also, any boilerplate amendment language that legal would accept would help speed things up.

Appreciate a couple of options and a rough timeline if we sign by Apr 28.

Thanks,
Asha
Head of Product, HelioMed
[Ext: +1 415 555 0199]
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha@heliomed.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-contract uplift — proposal and payment questions

Asha — thanks for the heads up, and congrats on the accelerated rollout. Short answers up front, then options below.

TL;DR: We can do both add-on (month-to-month) and an annualized pro-rate. We can also accept a split payment; terms and discount vary. Attached a pricing workbook with line-item math and a one-page amendment draft.

Options (all assume the current contract (Renewal: 2028-02-15) stays in force):

1) Month-to-month add-on (simplest)
   - Uplift priced at the published per-token rate for your tier (no change to existing discount ladder).
   - Billing monthly, cancellable at month-end. No commitment to annualize.
   - Payment: standard net-30 invoice (can split with two equal invoices in first billing cycle if needed).
   - Ideal if you want flexibility and low legal friction.

2) Annualize the uplift (recommended if you want better unit economics)
   - We convert the uplift into a 10-month pro-rated commit, then annualize to align with your Feb renewal. Example math in attachment: ~12% blended discount on uplift vs. M2M.
   - Billing: upfront for the 10-month pro-rate, or split into two invoices (May + Nov) with contract note that remaining balance is due upon Nov invoice.
   - Benefit: immediate lower unit cost; downside: more formal amendment and limited flexibility.

3) Hybrid (staged commitment)
   - 50% of uplift annualized, 50% kept M2M. Blend the billing and discount. Useful as a runway test.

Other notes:
- Legal: I've attached a proposed amendment draft. Monica (cc) is our renewal lead — she'll confirm standard legal language and whether DocuSign is acceptable for signature.
- Timing: If you confirm today, I can get a priced amendment and DocuSign envelope out by Apr 26; if you sign by Apr 28, we can target May 1 provisioning.

Attachments:
- pricing_calc_v2.xlsx (breakdown: per-token math, blended discounts, invoice schedule examples)
- proposed_amendment_draft.pdf (straightforward SOW + billing exhibit)

Next steps: let me know which option you prefer and whether HelioMed wants split invoices (May + Nov) or a single upfront pro-rate. If you want to push for a deeper discount we can escalate to Ben for an approval conversation.

Best,
Markus Klein
Senior Account Manager | Redwood Inference
m: +1 650 555 0122
[Attachment: pricing_calc_v2.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet, 42 KB)]
[Attachment: proposed_amendment_draft.pdf (PDF, 95 KB)]
From: Asha Rao <asha@heliomed.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Devon Li <devon@heliomed.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-contract uplift — proposal and payment questions

Markus — thanks for the quick turnaround and clear options. We ran the numbers with Finance and prefer the annualize option (Option 2) because of the unit cost, but Finance has two asks before we can sign:

1) Can Redwood extend a modest one-time uplift credit (we're asking for a 6% one-time credit on the uplift volume) because this is an accelerated go-live driven by product changes.
2) We'd like the invoice split to be May (50%) and Nov (50%) rather than full upfront. If the pro-rate requires more complex terms, we need that spelled out for our AP team.

If there is any flexibility on the one-time credit, I can push to get legal and AP to sign the amendment in parallel with a conditional PO.

Thanks — Asha
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha@heliomed.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-contract uplift — proposal and payment questions

Asha, Devon — appreciate the clarity and the context. Monica, Ben — looping you both in to confirm approval flow for a one-time uplift credit and split invoicing.

Response to HelioMed asks:
- Split invoices (May 50% / Nov 50%): acceptable. We'll reflect the schedule in the billing exhibit of the amendment and add the AP-friendly payment clause you requested.
- One-time uplift credit (6%): Ben, can we approve a promotional credit of 6% on the uplift volume for this specific SOW amendment? If not 6%, what ceiling can we offer without needing executive approval?

Monica: if legal is fine with the two-invoice approach and our billing ops can support the Nov follow-up invoice, I'll prepare the DocuSign envelope with the updated amendment. I've included the HubSpot deal and proposed DocuSign link below so we can track.

Next steps once Ben confirms credit:
1) I will update the pricing workbook and amendment.
2) I'll send a DocuSign link to Asha + Devon for signature and attach the PO field.
3) Once signed, billing will issue the May invoice (net-30) and schedule the Nov split invoice as a second charge; provisioning triggers on the May invoice receipt.

Thanks — Marku s
Markus Klein
Senior Account Manager | Redwood Inference
